(1) a dependency tree based feature set significantly improves URE performance, and (2) that the combination of URE and DCM produces a set of patterns that is more accurate than the original URE method.

In summary, our research is concerned with
two main contributions to the field of relation discovery: 1. A new method to generate informative features for clustering entity pairs in the vector space model, based on dependency trees.

the question of how to improve unsupervised relation extraction by using a discriminatively trained feature set, and how to extend the output of URE to produce discriminative relation-specific patterns.

In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
we have developed and evaluated a method for extracting relations from unstructured text that outperforms previous methods in both relation discovery and relation extraction.

we have shown that the combination of a feature selection method based on syntactic information and a pattern learning method based on Discriminative Category Matchings is a promising approach for the unsupervised discovery of relations and discriminative extraction patterns.

the proposed method outperforms the baseline in both the relation discovery task as well as the relation extraction task, and the proposed method outperforming the baseline in the relation discovery task is more than the baseline.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the proposed feature generation technique and the pattern extraction method significantly improve the URE performance, which is confirmed by the results in the experiments.
we have developed an unsupervised approach to extract relation instances from text.

the use of dependency trees in URE improves the quality of the discovered relations, and the application of discriminative category matching to the patterns improves the quality of information extraction.
The main takeaway from our work is that
a simple, unsupervised, and scalable approach can be used to find patterns that reliably evoke a relation and can be used to improve the performance of an information extraction system.

the combination of an informed feature generation method, an effective clustering method, and a discriminative pattern selection method is an important step towards the goal of fully unsupervised relation extraction.
the quality of URE can be greatly improved using an informed feature generation method, and that the patterns produced by URE are of sufficient quality to be used by an IE system.
